questions.question: In U.S. labor statistics, who is generally classified as unemployed?
choices: An adult without paid work, whether or not available or searching
A jobless person available for work who actively searched in the last four weeks
An adult working fewer than full-time hours, regardless of job preferences
An adult who receives less income than in the previous year

questions.question: What is the labor force?
choices: All residents including young children
Only people working full-time
Only people collecting unemployment benefits
People classified as employed plus unemployed

questions.question: How is the unemployment rate calculated?
choices: Unemployed people divided by the labor force
Unemployed people divided by total population
Employed people divided by total land area
Retired people divided by employed people

questions.question: What is frictional unemployment?
choices: Joblessness caused only by a national recession
Joblessness caused only by a mismatch of skills
Joblessness during transitions or searches between jobs
Joblessness caused only by seasonal weather

questions.question: What is structural unemployment?
choices: Joblessness during a brief ordinary job search only
Joblessness linked to a mismatch between workers and available jobs
Joblessness caused only by a holiday closure
Joblessness caused by leaving the workforce entirely

questions.question: What is cyclical unemployment?
choices: Joblessness associated with downturns in economic activity
Joblessness arising only from regular seasonal patterns
Joblessness during every voluntary job switch
Joblessness unrelated to changing demand

questions.question: What is seasonal unemployment?
choices: Joblessness caused only by technological replacement
Joblessness caused only by unexpected national recessions
Joblessness caused by permanent retirement
Joblessness related to predictable seasonal changes in work

questions.question: Why are discouraged workers generally excluded from the headline U.S. unemployment rate?
choices: They are automatically counted as full-time employees
They always receive wages from their former employers
They have stopped actively searching and are outside the labor force
They are counted only as business owners

questions.question: Why can someone working part-time still be considered employed?
choices: Employment status does not require full-time hours
Only jobs with health insurance count as employment
Part-time workers are always classified as unemployed
Employment requires a permanent contract

questions.question: How can a recession raise cyclical unemployment?
choices: Falling demand necessarily raises every wage
Falling demand can lead firms to reduce production and staffing
Businesses must expand staffing when sales decline
Recessions eliminate the need for economic statistics

questions.question: Why can training help address structural unemployment?
choices: It guarantees every worker an immediate job
It eliminates all seasonal patterns
It changes only the number of people collecting benefits
It may build skills suited to changing job requirements

questions.question: What is labor-force participation rate?
choices: Unemployed people as a share of employed people
Retirees as a share of all children
The labor force as a share of the relevant civilian population
Full-time workers as a share of exports

questions.question: Why are benefit claims not the same as the official count of unemployment?
choices: Some unemployed people do not qualify for or claim benefits
Every unemployed person automatically receives benefits
Only benefit recipients can search for work
Benefits count all people who are outside the labor force

questions.question: Why can an unemployment rate fall without more people finding jobs?
choices: Population must have become zero
Some jobless people may stop searching and leave the labor force
Every jobless person must have become employed
Businesses must have raised all wages

questions.question: Why do broader labor-market measures consider involuntary part-time work?
choices: Part-time workers are never included in employment
Broader measures count only business profits
Workers choose their hours freely in every case
The headline rate may not capture insufficient hours among employed workers

questions.question: A labor force has 10,000 people, including 500 unemployed. What is the unemployment rate?
A worker's job disappears because new production requires different skills. Which category fits best?
choices: Structural unemployment
Frictional unemployment alone
Seasonal unemployment
Voluntary retirement

questions.question: A worker leaves one job and searches for a better match. Which category fits best?
choices: Seasonal unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Cyclical unemployment necessarily
Permanent withdrawal from the labor force

questions.question: A ski resort reduces staff each spring under its regular schedule. Which category fits best?
choices: Structural unemployment necessarily
Frictional unemployment alone
Retirement
Seasonal unemployment

questions.question: A person has no job, wants work, but has not searched during the recent four-week period because jobs seem unavailable. Under standard U.S. classification, where does the person generally fall?
choices: Employed full-time
Unemployed solely because no job is held
Outside the labor force
Automatically counted as an employer
